text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:

-The Justice Department says Norway's patient association is not allowed to establish a register for doctors' qualifications. The department says such a listing could be unnecessarily detrimental to a doctor's reputation.
-The Foreign Ministry rejects recent accusations by Iranian newspapers that Norwegian authorities are led by the U.S.'s Central Intelligence Agency and that they harass Muslims living in Norway.
-The EU Commission has decided to postpone for another month an announcement of its conclusions of investigation into whether Norway has dumped salmon on the European market.

-Swedish Tricorona Mineral AB has found gold in mines north of Oslo. Tricorona manager Paul Hammergren says it is difficult to estimate how much gold the mines contain, but says he is convinced it is a large find.

-U.S. oil company, Mobil considers the Norwegian continental shelf (NCS) one of seven main areas for hydrocarbon resources. Mobil's Norwegian subsidiary, Mobil Exploration, plans to invest ten billion crowns on the NCS over the next five years.

-The government may decide to raise the state's stake in Scandinavian Airlines Systems (SAS) by buying shares from both the Danish and Swedish states. A governmental committee is looking at possibilities of investing part of the Petroleum Fund in air services.
